Exolum are an innovative fuel storage company with the priority of a green energy future operating globally. People are at the heart our expansion plans with a focus on developing our colleagues to reach their potential while accepting everyone as they are!

**IT Infrastructure Engineer- Flexible Site Location- 12 months FTC**

**About the role**

As part of the IT team, you will play a key role in maintaining and developing Exolum's Global IT infrastructure, ensuring systems remain secure, reliable and fit for business needs. You will support infrastructure projects, manage critical infrastructure services and act as a 3rd line escalation point for complex technical issues. Working closely with colleagues across the business and the wider Exolum Group, you will help deliver innovative and secure technology solutions that support operational excellence and future growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Manage and maintain the Exolum Global IT and OT infrastructure including Network and Communication Services (LAN, WAN, WIFI, SDWAN, ....), Infrastructure Services (Servers (Cloud, Onpremise), AD, Exchange....), and business applications.  Take operational ownership of assigned infrastructure services, monitoring availability, capacity, resilience, lifecycle, risks and improvement actions, and escalating investment or architectural decisions where required.
* Support the delivery of infrastructure projects (Local & Global) to allow the business to take advantage of shared standards and systems.
* Ensure projects completed are fully compliant with company policies, procedures and legal requirements, particularly safety.
* Ensure the security of services & projects is upheld throughout all infrastructure.
* Collaborate & Support the Infrastructure team in planning and implementing additions, deletions and major modifications to the supporting group infrastructure.
* To act as the escalation point for the in house 2nd Line engineer.
* Lead or coordinate infrastructure incidents, problems and changes in accordance with ITSM processes, including impact and risk assessment, implementation planning, rollback readiness, stakeholder communications and post-implementation validation.
* Ensure that all completed projects have as-built designs and procedures documented and all relevant databases are updated to hand over to the 1st and 2nd line support. Maintain accurate infrastructure asset, configuration and lifecycle information, including CMDB records, warranties, licences, support status, dependencies and end-of-life or end-of-support planning.
* Support the IT Manager and Senior IT Engineer in developing and ensure procedures are in place to diagnose a system and methods applied to perform a full or partial system recovery . Support the maintenance and testing of infrastructure resilience, backup, recovery and disaster recovery arrangements, ensuring that service dependencies, recovery procedures, responsibilities and evidence are documented and regularly reviewed.
* Recognise necessary improvements, proactively identify solutions to satisfy business needs and make appropriate recommendations
* Identify potential issues with services (operation) and projects in the delivery phase before they impact the organisation, informing as soon as possible, suggesting potential alternatives or fixes.
* Highlight areas of the IT and OT operations that can be automated and suggest potential strategies.
* Work with suppliers and project managers to ensure that projects are delivered in a safe, timely manner.
* Coordinate infrastructure suppliers and service providers, supporting quotations, renewals, warranties, purchasing activities and delivery assurance. Monitor supplier actions and challenge technical, commercial or service issues when required.
* Assess infrastructure demands and determine the appropriate delivery route, distinguishing between standard requests, changes, operational activities and projects, and providing estimates of effort, cost, dependencies and risk where required.
* Support infrastructure budgeting and purchasing activities by preparing technical requirements, validating quotations, identifying OPEX and CAPEX implications and providing cost and lifecycle information for regional planning.
* Prepare and deliver clear communications for infrastructure changes, incidents, risks and projects, adapting technical information for site management, business stakeholders, suppliers and end users.

**About You**

You will be an experienced IT professional with strong infrastructure engineering expertise and a proactive approach to problem solving. You will have experience supporting and developing enterprise IT environments, delivering infrastructure projects and maintaining secure, resilient systems. With excellent communication skills and a collaborative mindset, you will be comfortable working with colleagues, suppliers and stakeholders at all levels while balancing operational requirements with cyber security and business needs. You will also be willing and able to travel as required to support business operations, projects and stakeholder engagement. Spanish language skills are desirable but not essential.

**Competency model**

At Exolum we run a Competency Model which has been defined accordingly to our strategy, values and the geographies where we operate, making it a unique and exclusive document for Exolum. The competency Model is understood as the set of identifiable and measurable behaviours (skills, aptitudes and motivations, among others) that enable a person to achieve superior performance.

**We Care**- We anticipate, identify and solve the needs of our internal and external clients. - Level 3

**We Do**- We face opportunities and challenges with proactivity, energy and enthusiasm and we take responsibility for our actions - Level 3

**We Connect** - We listen, share information and communicate clearly, transparently and openly - Level 3

**We Include** - We welcome, respect and value the uniqueness of people. - Level 2

**We Get Together** -We actively collaborate with other people in achieving shared goals - Level 2

**We Trust** - We act with integrity and coherence with our values and we comply with the commitments acquired- Level 2

**We Think Different** - We contribute, explore and experiment with new approaches to challenges without fear of being wrong - Level 3

* Salary £40,000 - £45,000 depending on experience
* Pension – up to Employee 6% and Employer 9%
* Holiday –30 days per annum
* Personalised career development plans
* Single Private Health Insurance via BUPA
* Healthcare Cash Plan
* Life Assurance x5 and Disability insurance
* Wellbeing Initiatives
* Employee Resource Groups – EDI Group, Employee Forum, Wellbeing Committee
* Study support (if applicable)

The first step is to apply – please visit https://jobs.exolum.com/ to complete your application. Once your application has been reviewed, if you are successful, you will be invited to meet our amazing team and your potential new line manager for a face-to-face interview. Depending on the role, you may be required to attend a second stage interview so we can get to know you even more!

**About Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion**

Different people approach problems differently and we believe that diversity is the engine that fuels innovation. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to creating an inclusive environment where diverse voices are not only heard but also amplified. We recognise that our differences—when embraced with respect—drive smarter decisions, stronger performance, and a culture where everyone can be their authentic selves.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, neurodiversity or any other legally protected status.

We welcome individuals with disabilities and strive to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates. To request an accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please email: HumanResources@exolum.com

We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. All applications are reviewed fairly and equally using a third-party blind recruiting solution (MeVitae) which removes any bias parameters.

## **What role you will play on our team**

Join a high performing Front Office Valuation and Structuring quant team supporting Gas and Power trading, asset optimization and structured transactions. You will provide transparent, independent and commercially actionable valuation expertise, with a strong focus on identifying, modelling and pricing embedded physical and financial optionality across storages, swing contracts, transportation/pipeline capacity and power generation assets.

Your work will support traders, originators and senior stakeholders in evaluating structured supply/offtake agreements, capacity deals, dispatch linked structures and cross commodity strategies, while contributing to global corporate initiatives requiring rigorous valuation, optionality analysis and risk translation beyond the core Trading organization.

## **What you will do**

* Provide fair valuation and independent risk assessment for gas storage, swing options, pipeline capacity rights, load following structures and power asset linked deals, quantifying operational, volume, flexibility and market optionality.
* Support traders and originators with structure design, including exercise rules, dispatch/flow logic, strike/index formulas, exposure mapping, sensitivities and commercial explanation of optionality value drivers.
* Build valuation templates and analytics tools capable of modelling storage injection/withdrawal optimization, swing flexibility, dispatch optionality and capacity arbitrage, using stochastic, scenario based and optimisation techniques.
* Contribute optionality and valuation insight to large global corporate projects, such as long term gas supply frameworks, optimization of cross border capacity, and power asset commercialisation initiatives.
* Advise on hedging strategies for complex exposures across gas hubs (NBP, TTF, Henry Hub), power markets, capacity rights and cross commodity structures, identifying hedgeable and residual components.
* Conduct back testing, assumption validation and parameter research, including calibration of illiquid curves, volatility structures, correlation frameworks and dispatch driven price dynamics.
* Collaborate with quant modelling/technology/data teams to ensure robust model deployment, integration into FO tools, and support for asset optimisation workflows.

Overview
We're looking for a Data Science Manager who can turn commercial problems into scalable Data Science products. 

You'll work closely with business and marketing teams to identify high-value opportunities, lead the development of reusable predictive models, and ensure those models become embedded in how the business makes decisions. 

This is a player-coach role. You'll lead and develop a growing team of Data Scientists while remaining close enough to the work to shape methodology, review technical outputs and contribute hands-on where needed. Your success won't be measured by how many models the team builds, but by how widely they're used and the commercial impact they create. 

The Opportunity
You'll work closely with the Director of Data Science to turn our Data Science strategy into scalable products and measurable business outcomes. You'll manage the day-to-day work of a growing team while partnering directly with stakeholders across the business to understand the decisions they're trying to make and identify where Data Science can materially improve the outcome. 

Our Data Science team works at the intersection of customer intelligence, performance marketing and commercial decision making. Initial areas of focus include lifetime value, propensity modelling, customer value, forecasting and marketing optimisation, including how predictive models can improve bidding and acquisition across platforms such as Google and Meta. 

This is not a research-focused role. We want someone who enjoys solving difficult modelling problems but is equally interested in what happens afterwards: how a model gets into production, how people use it, what we learn from it and whether it actually improves performance. 

What You'll Do 
Commercial & Decision Science 
Work with the Director of Data Science and business and marketing teams to identify high-value opportunities for Data Science, translating commercial problems into predictive models and decision-making products. You'll focus on areas including lifetime value, propensity modelling, customer value, forecasting and performance marketing optimisation, with commercial impact at the centre of how work is prioritised. 
Scalable Data Science Products 
Guide the development of reusable models and methodologies that can scale across products, verticals and use cases rather than repeatedly solving the same problems. You'll take work from experimentation through adoption, ensuring outputs are measurable, explainable and designed around how they'll ultimately be used. 
Production Data Science 
Work closely with Engineering and ML Ops to turn successful modelling work into reliable production products. You'll ensure models have appropriate experimentation, monitoring, retraining and feedback loops, while partnering with technical teams on the infrastructure needed to operate them at scale. 
Business Partnership & Insight 
Build trusted relationships across Marketing, Commercial, Analytics, Product and Engineering. You'll translate business needs into Data Science opportunities and complex modelling into clear recommendations, ensuring the team goes beyond producing predictions to explain what they mean, what we can learn from them and what the business should do next. 
Team Leadership & Technical Quality 
Lead and develop a growing team of Data Scientists while remaining technically close to the work. You'll coach the global team, review modelling approaches and technical outputs, establish consistent standards and contribute hands-on where it adds value. You'll create an environment where technical rigour, curiosity and commercial thinking reinforce one another. 

What You'll Bring
We're looking for someone who combines strong technical Data Science experience with the commercial judgement and communication skills needed to put it into practice. 

You'll likely bring: 
Experience managing and developing Data Scientists while remaining comfortable working at a technical level. 
Strong experience in predictive modelling, machine learning and customer analytics. 
Experience applying Data Science to commercial or performance marketing problems, ideally including LTV, propensity, customer value or acquisition optimisation. 
Strong Python and SQL skills and experience working within modern cloud-based Data Science environments. 
Experience taking models beyond experimentation and working with Engineering or ML Ops teams to deploy and operate them in production. 
Strong understanding of experimentation and model evaluation, with experience in incrementality or causal inference particularly valuable. 
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical work into clear recommendations for senior business audiences. 
A product mindset, with an interest in building reusable capabilities rather than one-off models. 
Strong commercial judgement and a focus on measuring the real-world impact of Data Science. 

Nice to Have
Experience in any of the following would be valuable, but we don't expect every candidate to bring all of them: 
Performance marketing and optimisation across Google, Meta or other major advertising platforms. 
Value-based bidding or conversion-value optimisation. 
Direct collaboration with advertising platform Data Science or Marketing Science teams. 
Affiliate marketing, lead generation or digital publishing. 
Financial services, insurance, health or other regulated industries. 
Attribution and marketing measurement. 
Forecasting commercial or marketing performance. 
DSP or advertising optimisation algorithms. 
Modern MLOps tooling and platforms such as Vertex AI. 
Applied AI techniques that complement traditional predictive modelling and decision science. 

Why Join Us? 
This is an opportunity to help build a Data Science capability where models are expected to do something. 

You'll work on commercially significant problems with large datasets, direct connections to marketing and customer outcomes, and a clear route from experimentation into production. You'll have the opportunity to shape how those problems are solved, lead a growing team and work alongside experienced leaders across Data Science, Engineering, Analytics, Product and the wider business. 

Most importantly, you'll be judged on the decisions your team improves and the value its products create, not simply the sophistication or number of models it builds.

**Location: Central London (Marylebone), some flexibility to work from home**

**Roster: Monday to Friday**

**Engagement Model: Direct Employee, ongoing**

Provide dedicated, principal-level contracts and procurement support to Energy & Growth Corporate Services from the United Kingdom.

The role works closely with stakeholders to give timely, practical support across sourcing, contracting and supplier matters, while maintaining independent procurement oversight and ensuring decisions and activity comply with Fortescue policies, delegated authorities and applicable governance requirements.

The role leads complex and high-value work provides senior commercial advice and maintains C&P assurance across stakeholder-led procurement. The role works autonomously within delegated authority and escalates decisions outside that authority.

* Build effective working relationships with Energy & Growth Corporate Services stakeholders and understand their priorities, delivery plans, budgets and risks.
* Provide responsive, practical advice on procurement routes, sourcing timelines, market options, commercial strategy and required approvals so that stakeholders can plan and make informed decisions.
* Prepare and maintain procurement plans and sourcing strategies for assigned requirements, aligned with business objectives, delivery schedules, budgets and Fortescue policy.

* Apply sound commercial judgement to balance value, risk, quality, delivery, resilience and sustainability considerations.

* Identify opportunities to improve commercial outcomes, reduce cost and avoid unnecessary complexity across the assigned portfolio.

* Use Fortescue procurement and enterprise systems consistently, promoting accurate data, timely approvals and reliable records.
* Contribute to improvements in C&P processes, guidance, templates and stakeholder capability, sharing lessons across Energy & Growth and the wider C&P function.

* Strong knowledge of strategic sourcing, tendering, commercial negotiation, contract formation, supplier management and procurement governance.
* Experience supporting stakeholders with competing priorities while protecting fair process, value for money and controls.

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. ## Job Description

**About this role:**

This is a pivotal, high-impact individual contributor role focused on driving rapid channel expansion, joint go-to-market strategy, and enterprise revenue growth across the UK and European region. As a Channel Sales Manager, you will be responsible for hunting, building, and scaling our Systems Integrator (SI) and Managed Service Provider (MSP) ecosystem.

Rather than simply managing existing accounts, this role requires a true intrapreneur and builder who can establish new partner practices from scratch. You will execute a comprehensive sell to, sell through, and sell with motion—recruiting and activating key partners with large existing books of business in incumbent IT Service Management (ITSM) tech stacks, creating a clear migration path to our modern SaaS platform.

The ideal candidate combines a high-energy hunter instinct with the commercial and technical acumen required to structure complex managed service programs, co-sell frameworks, buyouts, and pre-buy models.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Partner Recruitment & Practice Building (Hunt & Build)**

* Target & Recruit: Identify, target, and sign regional/large SIs and MSPs (specifically those managing a 50M–200M book of business in incumbent ITSM platforms).
* Sell To, Through & With Execution: Drive full-spectrum partner engagement—orchestrating Sell To (internal consumption/MSP platform licenses), Sell Through (partner resale/pre-buys), and Sell With (joint enterprise co-selling) revenue streams.
* Build Mid-Market & Low-Enterprise Practices: Partner with SI practice leads to establish new mid-market and enterprise delivery practices centered around our solution as the primary vendor of choice.
* Develop Displacement Off-Ramps: Create structured migration plans and compelling commercial business cases that enable partners to transition disenfranchised customers off legacy incumbent platforms.
* Complex Deal Structuring: Architect and execute sophisticated partnership agreements, including Managed Service Provider (MSP) programs, pre-buys, and buyouts.

**Enablement, Co-Sell & Program Governance**

* Co-Sell Framework Development: Design, roll out, and execute structured co-sell frameworks and joint go-to-market strategies that align partner sales reps with internal field AE teams on targeted enterprise accounts.
* High-Impact Onboarding & Enablement: Design partner onboarding and enablement models that directly reduce time-to-revenue, increase conversion velocity, and measurably improve win rates on complex enterprise opportunities.
* Autonomous Execution: Build and run partner programs autonomously without requiring extensive corporate infrastructure or existing playbook support—establishing new processes where none currently exist.
* Multi-Threaded Alignment: Engage across all levels of partner organizations—from practice leads and alliance directors to executive leadership—to secure go-to-market investment and dedicated engineering/GTM resources.

**Pipeline & Enterprise Revenue Ownership**

* Revenue Accountability: Own a post-ramp annual productivity target of ~$2M+, driving joint GTM strategy, pipeline growth, and enterprise revenue through high-velocity partner deals and strategic pre-buy investments.
* Pipeline Generation & Governance: Drive both partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, holding partners accountable through joint account planning, pipeline reviews, and structured QBRs.
* Value-Based Positioning: Clearly articulate a strong philosophical and commercial point of difference versus legacy competitors, positioning our platform as the modern, high-agility alternative.

## Qualifications

**Required Experience & Competencies**

* 7+ Years in SaaS Channel & Alliances: Proven track record in channel management, SI/MSP recruitment, joint GTM execution, or alliance development within an enterprise software environment.
* Full-Spectrum GTM Mastery: Hands-on experience executing sell to, sell through, and sell with motions, developing co-sell frameworks, and driving joint account planning with field teams.
* Onboarding & Enablement Innovation: Demonstrated track record of designing partner enablement programs that measurably shorten sales cycles, accelerate time-to-first-deal, and improve enterprise win rates.
* Managed Service & Program Structuring: Hands-on experience structuring, negotiating, and launching Managed Service Programs, pre-buys, and complex SI delivery models.
* Incumbent Ecosystem Knowledge: Deep operational understanding of legacy enterprise ITSM/CX ecosystems and how large partners structure, monetize, and deliver their practices.
* Building from Zero: Demonstrated ability to build net-new partner practices and GTM motions from scratch rather than inheriting mature, pre-packaged programs.
* Commercial Rigor: Exceptional commercial acumen with experience managing multi-million dollar quota targets and holding partners accountable to firm investment commitments.
* Senior Stakeholder Credibility: Ability to command respect and build immediate trust with senior leadership, practice heads, and C-level executives at major SIs and MSPs.

**Preferred Experience**

* Direct experience competing against or displacing major legacy enterprise ITSM platforms.
* Prior experience working within a fast-scaling, high-velocity SaaS startup environment where adaptability and speed are critical.
* Existing, active relationships across the UK and European regional SI and MSP community.

**Key Personal Attributes**

* Outcome-Focused Mindset: A tenacious self-starter who thrives in fast-paced, chaotic, or ambiguous environments and focuses entirely on driving execution, pipeline growth, and enterprise revenue over process for process's sake.
* Builder Mentality: Possesses the passion and grit of an entrepreneur, eager to leave a mark by designing the blueprint for the organization's enterprise channel motion.
* High Pace & Executive Gravitas: Combines speed of execution with professional presence, compelling communication, and strong storytelling ability.
* Adaptable & Pragmatic: Unafraid to break, fix, or reinvent internal processes to solve partner problems and close deals

**Network Architect**

We’re looking for an accomplished Network Architect to join our Scalable Tech Team at Genomics England and provide technical leadership for the secure, resilient connectivity that underpins our technology platform, healthcare, research and corporate services.

Our network services connect cloud platforms (primarily AWS) and on-premise infrastructure, enabling clinicians, researchers and colleagues to access sensitive genomic and associated health data securely and reliably.

Working within the Technology and Product Directorate, you’ll shape and deliver Genomics England’s network architecture across AWS, hybrid connectivity, corporate locations and partner integrations. You’ll collaborate with infrastructure, cloud platform, security, engineering, procurement, commercial, service management and delivery colleagues to turn complex operational and user needs into coherent, cost-effective, scalable and secure network solutions.

This is an architecture role where you’ll balance longer-term network strategy with practical delivery. Drawing on your proven experience as an Architect, you will guide teams through network architecture decisions, develop reusable standards and patterns, and ensure solutions align with Genomics England’s wider technology strategy, architecture standards, security requirements and service expectations.

The scale and sensitivity of genomics require high-performing, highly available networks. AWS is at the heart of our environment, alongside hybrid and third-party connectivity, supporting secure data transfer, high-performance compute, large-scale storage, research workflows, operational services and controlled access to sensitive data.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the architecture and design of network solutions across Genomics England, ensuring they are secure, scalable, cost-effective, resilient, supportable and aligned with organisational needs. Define target architectures, standards and reusable patterns for cloud, hybrid, remote-access and partner connectivity.
* Design and govern AWS networking, including multi-account connectivity, VPC design, routing, segmentation, private connectivity, DNS, load balancing and network security controls. Architect resilient connectivity between AWS, Genomics England locations, NHS and government partners, research organisations, suppliers and other trusted environments.
* Work with security colleagues to embed zero-trust principles, least privilege, network segmentation, secure remote access, encryption in transit and effective boundary protection. Ensure network designs support the secure movement and processing of large-scale genomic and associated health data, including high-throughput and latency-sensitive workloads.
* Develop network roadmaps and transition architectures that balance strategic direction, technical debt, service continuity and delivery priorities. Provide architectural oversight from discovery and options analysis through implementation, migration and live service.
* Document network architectures, traffic flows, trust boundaries, technical options, decisions, dependencies and transition states clearly for technical and non-technical audiences. Define requirements for network observability, performance monitoring, capacity management, configuration control, resilience testing and incident response.
* Collaborate with cloud platform, infrastructure, engineering, security, service management and delivery teams to ensure designs can be implemented and operated effectively. Contribute to architecture governance and assurance, presenting network designs and recommendations through appropriate technical forums.
* Identify network risks, constraints, dependencies and single points of failure early, working with teams to address them. Evaluate emerging networking technologies and managed services where they could improve security, performance, resilience, operability or cost-effectiveness.
* Work with architects across Genomics England to create coherent end-to-end solutions and encourage appropriate reuse across services. Contribute to architecture best practice and improving the quality of architecture across Genomics England.

**Skills and Experience for Success**

* Substantial experience designing and delivering enterprise network architectures in complex, security-conscious environments, with strong knowledge of AWS networking services and patterns, including VPCs, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, VPN, Route 53, load balancing, private endpoints and network security controls.
* Experience designing hybrid and multi-site connectivity, routing, switching, segmentation, firewalls, DNS, IP address management, load balancing and secure remote access. Detailed knowledge of physical network technology, ideally Cisco, NVIDIA and Mellanox, and in-depth understanding of Cisco Nexus Dashboard, data centre fabrics, Aruba networking infrastructure, BGP, OSPF, RoCE v2, performance optimisation and lifecycle management.
* Experience architecting highly available and resilient networks with clear recovery objectives, diverse connectivity and tested failover arrangements. Strong understanding of network security architecture, zero-trust principles, defence in depth, trust boundaries and secure connectivity to third parties.
* Experience designing networks for high-throughput, data-intensive or latency-sensitive workloads and diagnosing performance or capacity constraints. Good understanding of automation, infrastructure as code, configuration management, observability and operational support for modern networks.
* Ability to translate business, security, operational and user needs into practical network designs, standards and delivery roadmaps, balancing strategic architectural direction with immediate delivery needs, legacy constraints and service continuity.
* Experience working with multidisciplinary teams and building alignment across architecture, infrastructure, cloud, engineering, security, procurement, commercial, service management and delivery stakeholders. Strong stakeholder engagement and a collaborative approach that builds trust and supports effective decision-making.
* Experience documenting and communicating network architectures, traffic flows, options, risks and decisions clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, and providing architectural governance and assurance throughout the delivery lifecycle.
* Ability to identify where network architecture practices, standards or controls could be improved and to embed those improvements into regular use.

**Desirable Skills and Experience**

* Relevant professional certification, such as AWS Advanced Networking, AWS Solutions Architect, Cisco CCNP/CCIE or an equivalent qualification.
* Experience working in healthcare, genomics, research, government or another regulated environment handling sensitive data, and experience in procurement processes associated with network infrastructure in a UK government organisation.
* Experience with software-defined networking, SD-WAN, secure access service edge, network access control or zero-trust network access. Knowledge of AWS Network Firewall, Cloud WAN, VPC Lattice, Gateway Load Balancer and related network security or connectivity services.
* Experience designing connectivity for high-performance compute, large-scale storage, data transfer appliances or distributed data-processing environments, and integrating with NHS, government, academic, research or commercial partner networks.
* Knowledge of network telemetry and tooling, including flow logs, packet analysis, synthetic monitoring, performance analytics and security monitoring.
* Experience with DevOps practices, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, automation and policy as code for network services.
* Understanding of identity-aware networking, certificate services, encryption, proxies, web gateways and data-loss prevention controls.
* Experience contributing to architecture governance forums such as a Technical Design Authority, familiarity with enterprise architecture tools such as Abacus, and experience applying TOGAF or equivalent architecture practices.

If you’re an experienced Network Architect who enjoys solving complex connectivity and security challenges, this is an exciting opportunity to shape the secure, resilient networks spanning AWS, on-premises infrastructure and partner environments that support life-changing genomic healthcare and research at Genomics England.

The most important thing is that you care deeply about customers and can move fast without losing quality. You are a strong practitioner; you can go from whiteboard to high-fidelity quickly, and you know when each is appropriate.

Significant experience as a product designer, with a portfolio that demonstrates complex UX problem-solving; not just polished visuals.

Strong product thinking; you can define the problem, question the brief, and help decide what to build, not just how it should look.

Experience designing for security, developer, or enterprise SaaS products.

Background working at an early-stage startup where you built things from scratch.

AI agents are changing how companies operate, and the question of how to govern them safely is only going to grow. Geordie is building the platform enterprises rely on to answer that question.

You will join at a point where design is still being defined. There is no legacy system to work around, no established playbook to follow; just a hard problem, a sharp team, and a genuine opportunity to shape how a new category is understood.

You will work with real customers, see the impact of your work quickly, and have the scope to grow as the company does.

We listen intently and stay focused on what truly matters to our customers. If it doesn't help them navigate real-world agentic adoption and risk, it's probably not worth building.

We favour momentum over perfection; testing, learning, and evolving through action. It's how we move fast and get better, together.

We're honest, respectful, and unafraid to challenge each other. We believe doing great work should feel good, too. Kindness makes that possible.

**A Platform for Your Best Work**

We want this to be the most meaningful chapter of your career. Geordie is the place where you grow, lead and lift others, while building something that truly matters.

As the Director of Dedicated Infrastructure Engineering & Platforms, you will lead the engineering organization responsible for GitLab Dedicated, GitLab's premium single-tenant SaaS offering for enterprise customers in regulated industries, and public sector.

You will lead a high-performing organization of managers and engineers who own the entire lifecycle of dedicated and cellular platforms, from orchestration, integrations, resilience, and incident response to switchboard APIs, public sector compliance, and enterprise customer migrations. As a high-impact executive leader, you will define the strategy for single-tenant and public sector SaaS platforms, drive critical infrastructure investments, ensure FedRAMP/compliance operational readiness, and build the switchboard and migration capabilities that allow enterprise customers to seamlessly transition to and scale on Dedicated. You will succeed by cultivating a culture of operational excellence, closing key business and roadmap gaps, and leading distributed engineering teams to deliver high-availability, highly secure platform experiences.

## **What you'll do**

* Own the strategy and roadmap for GitLab Dedicated, and ensure the platform scales with customer growth and converges with GitLab's cellular architecture.

* Hire, coach, and scale engineering managers across distributed teams, and bring practical AI-enabled workflows into how the organization works.
* Partner with Product, Security, and Customer Support to keep customer commitments, architecture, and investments aligned.

# DevOps Engineer - UK

Norwich, England, United Kingdom

### **The Company**

Glassbox's mission is to empower enterprises to shape trusted, frictionless digital experiences.

Glassbox is a leading force in shaping digital experiences. It helps organizations uncover digital issues, boost conversion rates, enhance accessibility, prevent fraud, and more. Leveraging AI-driven customer intelligence, Glassbox enables enterprises to deliver secure, proactive, and preventative digital experiences. Its solutions are trusted by highly regulated organizations, including SoFi, Cal, and many others. We are growing and have been recognized by G2 as one of 2024's Top 50 Software Companies in the world.

Glassbox is looking for a DevOps Engineer to join our global team.

### **What You Will do?**

You will work with cutting-edge technologies and tackle a wide range of challenges in building a **scalable, globally distributed infrastructure**.  
In this role, you will:

* Work with a diverse set of technologies, simplifying complex solutions.
* Collaborate closely with multiple teams across the organization.
* Be part of a team responsible for designing, optimizing, and maintaining a **high-scale production environment** that handles massive traffic loads with high complexity.
* **Architect, deploy, and maintain** robust and scalable cloud infrastructures on ***AWS*** **and Azure**.
* **Develop and optimize CI/CD pipelines** to support automated deployment, testing, and scaling across multiple environments.
* **Implement and manage monitoring, logging, and alerting solutions** across cloud platforms to ensure application health and performance.
* Provide **advanced troubleshooting and resolution** for infrastructure issues in production, development, and testing environments.

**What You Will Need?**

* **4+ years of experience** in a ***DevOps*** or related engineering role, with a strong background in ***AWS*** and cloud-native environments. Proven ability to design, manage, and maintain **high-scale production systems**, ensuring **reliability, performance, and scalability**.
* **Deep expertise in cloud technologies and application security**, with a strong focus on **best practices for securing resilient, scalable, and cost-efficient architectures**.
* **Extensive experience** with **containerization and orchestration technologies**, including ***Docker*****,** ***Kubernetes*****, and Helm**.
* **Proficiency in automation tools** such as **Terraform**, and hands-on experience with **CI/CD pipelines** using tools like **Jenkins**.
* **Strong knowledge of monitoring and logging tools** (e.g., **Prometheus, Grafana, Loki**) to ensure system health, optimize performance, and proactively detect issues.
* **Proficiency in scripting languages** (e.g., **Node.js,** ***Bash***) to automate workflows and enhance operational efficiency.
* **Excellent communication, collaboration, and documentation skills**, with a proactive approach to problem-solving.
* **Passionate about learning** new technologies and tackling **complex challenges** in a fast-paced environment.
* **Hands-on experience managing big data infrastructure**, optimizing performance and scalability for data-intensive applications.

**Preferred**

* **Proficiency in database technologies**, including **Cassandra, Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, and PostgreSQL HA**.
* **Expertise in Kafka cluster administration**, including **cross-region replication** and high-availability configurations.
* **Experience with MLOps workflows and infrastructure**, including model deployment, monitoring, and scaling in production environments.

## About the Role

We are looking for a highly experienced Link Tutor to join our pastoral support team, working alongside our existing Link Tutors to support students in Key Stages 3 and 4.

The Link Tutor role is varied and hugely rewarding. You will join a highly motivated, creative and experienced team committed to ensuring that children and young people are able to access education despite the health barriers they may be facing.

The role has a strong pastoral focus. Link Tutors provide individualised support to help students engage with their education while they are with us and, wherever possible, successfully transition back to their mainstream school, an alternative provision or their post-16 destination.

Regular contact with students, including visits to their homes, is a fundamental part of the role. These visits enable Link Tutors to build strong relationships with students, identify barriers to learning, recognise key milestones, develop strategies and skills, and support aspects of our wellbeing curriculum. Student voice is central to this work and to the decisions made about the support each young person needs.

Link Tutors work closely with parents and carers, mainstream schools, GHES teaching staff and the wider network of professionals supporting each young person. This includes liaison with Social Care and medical professionals, as well as attendance at meetings such as TAF, Child in Need (CIN), Child Protection (CP), PEP and Graduated Pathway meetings.

As GHES is a short-term service, transition and reintegration are key features of the role. Link Tutors have an important part to play in facilitating carefully planned and supported transitions, working collaboratively with the student, family, school and other professionals to achieve the best possible outcome.

We are looking for candidates who have experience of working with children and young people with additional needs and who understand the importance of effective multi-agency working.

* understand the Graduated Pathway and the importance of a student-centred approach;

## Job Description

**Position Summary**

Why join our team?

We are expanding our team of privacy experts to support the Samsung Electronics’ European Service Business (“ESBO”).

ESBO processes large quantities of Samsung’s first-party data and third-party data to provide consumers with Samsung services on Samsung mobiles and Samsung Smart TVs in Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA). The data is especially relevant to our advertising business, Samsung Ads, where Samsung data is its unique selling proposition.

To manage these risks, Samsung has a global team of privacy experts. They are integral to the continued success of Samsung’s new and existing products.

Given the importance of consumer trust, Samsung is a privacy-forward company. We are focused on making sure that our consumers’ personal data is treated fairly and within the scope of relevant data protection legislation.

We are looking for a Senior Privacy Manager – Consent & Transparency to join our rapidly growing advertising and services business as an integral part of our data privacy and compliance function for EMEA Service Business.

You will lead the privacy side of a new ESBO consent and transparency framework and support the team on general privacy matters across ESBO.

The successful applicant will report into the Director of Privacy – EMEA and will be based in central London. Some travel may be required. You will work in close partnership with the Product team, who owns the product roadmap and delivery of the framework.

**Role and Responsibilities**

**Your key responsibilities**

As a Privacy Manager, you will be the business’s expert on consent, transparency and device-level tracking. This role sits outside the legal team but works closely with product teams, engineering, legal and leadership to embed privacy-by-design and default principles into our operations.

You will be responsible for guiding the business on consent and transparency risk and ethical data use, ensuring our products not only comply with GDPR, ePrivacy/PECR and TCF requirements, but also give consumers a real, informed choice that they understand and can change.

The key responsibilities of this role will be to:

* Lead the privacy and compliance workstream for a device-level TCF CMP – consent design, purposes and vendor scope, legal QA of consent journeys, and sign-off gates from design through to rollout.
* Own ongoing TCF and regulatory compliance for the CMP once live, including CMP registration and validation, Global Vendor List management, vendor onboarding and removal, and monitoring of TCF policy and version changes.
* Own our existing consent mechanisms and transparency products, including privacy notices, first-run and in-device disclosures and user preference controls, keeping them accurate as our products and data flows change.
* Conduct and document data protection impact assessments and legitimate interest assessments for consent-dependent initiatives, including audience measurement (JIC) participation and programmatic advertising products.
* Maintain a market-by-market view of consent and device-storage requirements across EMEA, tracking regulator guidance and national ePrivacy implementations, and translating changes into product requirements.
* Work in close partnership with Product & GTM, converting legal and regulatory requirements into clear product specifications, acceptance criteria and release sign-off.
* Assist our partnerships and legal colleagues to on-board new clients, service providers, AdTech vendors and data partners in a privacy compliant and efficient manner.
* Assist in the creation, implementation and management of business mandates and privacy processes to ensure policy and regulatory compliance, and maintain privacy-related documentation including records of processing, compliance logs and approvals.
* Design, develop and assist with the delivery of business-specific training on consent, transparency and TCF for internal stakeholders.
* Support the wider privacy programme on ad hoc matters as workload requires, including business requests, new product reviews and data subject rights requests.
* Streamline privacy workflows, leveraging automation and AI tools where applicable.

**What we need for this role**

To be successful, you will possess the following skills and attributes:

* Deep understanding of GDPR, ePrivacy/PECR and other EMEA privacy laws, with particular depth on consent, transparency, and the rules on storing or accessing information on a user’s device.
* Working knowledge of the IAB Europe Transparency and Consent Framework (TCF v2.2) – purposes and legal bases, the TC String, the Global Vendor List and CMP validation.
* Hands-on experience of consent management in practice – implementing, configuring, operating or directly advising on a consent management platform – and a working understanding of how consent signals are captured, stored and passed downstream.
* Proven track record of successfully managing data protection compliance and implementing privacy-by-design principles across multiple jurisdictions, including data protection impact assessments and legitimate interest assessments.
* Ability to work credibly with product and engineering teams: turning legal requirements into specifications that can be built, and reviewing what is built against what was agreed.
* Ability to quickly and accurately assess practical and business risks in a fast-paced environment and the ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organisation.
* Demonstrated success in managing multiple high-priority projects simultaneously, coordinating seamlessly across global teams and functions.
* Exceptional interpersonal skills and an absolute commitment to professionalism and collegiality.
* Maintain composure under pressure with a positive, solutions-oriented attitude and collaborative spirit.

Additional desirable skills and attributes which are not necessary, but will be helpful to the role:

* Industry expertise in media, broadcasting, advertising or marketing, combined with privacy knowledge; connected TV or streaming experience is particularly welcome.

## Job description

**About the role:**

Greyparrot builds AI-powered waste analytics — software that identifies and quantifies material streams in real time, delivered through analysers we design and manufacture. Hardware and software are equally core to the product: the analysers exist to feed the software, and the software is only as good as hardware that ships on time, works reliably, and scales with demand.

We are moving out of an R&D-volume phase into steady, operationalised production — roughly 150 units built in 2026, with 2027 volumes forecast at 500+. Analysers are built by a production partner based in Wales, using parts sourced from Asia & Europe, and shipped to customers across the US, Europe, and the UK. Right now, production ownership is split: forecasting and budget approval sit with the COO, while purchasing, including placing parts orders and fielding supplier and production-partner queries, has defaulted to the Hardware Manager, who knows the suppliers best but needs to return to R&D. Neither is a dedicated supply chain role, which makes this a function that can't scale independently of either of them.

This role exists to take that ownership on properly: the production partner relationship, the parts pipeline that feeds it, the ERP that tracks all of it, and the supplier and freight relationships that determine what it costs, including outbound and returns flows. Stock and order tracking is manual today, and a first version of the ERP will be stood up before you start. You take it over from day one and own it from there: what it holds, how well it fits, and how it grows with volume. This role sits alongside the Logistics & Delivery Lead, who owns shipment booking, last-mile delivery, and on-site installation. This role owns carrier contracts and rates, customs, and returns, plus the planning, forecasting, and partner management that everything downstream depends on, and the handover between the two is explicit.

**Mission**

*To ensure Greyparrot always has the analysers, parts, and shipping capacity to meet demand - on time, at a defensible cost - as production scales from early stage volumes into growth scale.*

**Outcomes**

These are the results you will be held to. How you achieve them is yours to figure out.

* **Production and stock are actively managed, not tracked after the fact.** Iota’s build schedule, work-in-progress, and finished-goods stock are managed against real, current demand — the business is never caught short of analysers to ship, and never sitting on cash tied up in stock it doesn’t need yet. Stock is held within Iota’s holding limit (currently around 50 units), with a third-party logistics provider (3PL) for anything that needs to sit beyond it.
* **Parts arrive before they’re needed, not when they’re missed.** Global parts orders — mostly from Asia — are placed against a rolling forecast that respects real lead times (currently around 18 weeks), so a line ramp or a demand spike never stalls production because an order went in too late. Orders within the agreed purchasing budget are yours to approve; only spend above it goes to the COO.
* **Capacity is a known number, not a guess.** Production capacity — build rate, ramp time, and refurbishment throughput — is forecast against the sales pipeline and board targets, so Operations and Commercial always know what can actually be built and shipped, and by when, without needing to ask.
* **Stock, orders, and production status are visible across the business, in a system you own.** You own the ERP that replaces today’s manual tracking — its requirements, configuration, data quality, adoption, and ongoing administration, and the roadmap for it as volume grows — so the current picture of parts, stock, and production is visible to whoever needs it, whenever they need it.
* **Supplier economics are actively managed, not accepted as given.** Rates with the parts suppliers and shipping providers are benchmarked and renegotiated on a regular cycle, keeping landed cost per unit under control as volume scales.
* **Commercial demand drives purchasing only when it’s firm.** Forecasts and reserves from Commercial turn into purchase orders and dispatch only once there is a signed contract and a completed site-readiness form, so parts and units aren’t committed against demand that doesn’t land.
* **Product version changes land cleanly.** When a new analyser version or bill of materials replaces the current one, the cutover is planned across parts, stock, and Iota’s build schedule, so old-version parts aren’t left stranded and the new version isn’t held up waiting for them.
* **Returned and refurbished units flow back into supply deliberately.** Returned units are tracked, assessed, and either refurbished and restocked or retired, with their costs and customs treatment accounted for, so the refurbishment stream adds supply rather than confusion.
* **Outbound logistics is reliable in every market we ship to.** Shipments to the US, Europe, and UK are planned and executed to account for each region’s customs, duties, and documentation requirements, so delivery timelines hold and nothing gets stuck at a border; returns are tracked against outbound shipments so customs and duties reconcile.
* **A single point of failure doesn’t stay a single point of failure.** The risk of relying on one production partner and long parts lead times is named explicitly, with real mitigations in place — buffer stock, an escalation path, and a live plan to qualify a second production partner (likely US-based) so the business isn’t exposed to one site, one region, or one relationship.
* **Hardware, Finance, and Commercial all work from the same picture.** Production status, capacity constraints, and cost data are visible and current for the teams that plan around them, without each function needing a separate update. And, Hardware's time goes to R&D, not purchasing or supplier calls.

**Competencies**

How you work matters as much as what you deliver. These reflect Greyparrot's values, at Senior IC tier.

**CURIOSITY**

You build a culture of asking why in the supply chain — why a forecast missed, why a part slipped, why a supplier's price moved — and you encourage Hardware, Finance, and Commercial to ask the same of you. You're willing to be wrong and to update your view publicly when new evidence warrants it, whether that's a supplier, a forecast, or how the ERP is set up, and you share your reasoning where others can see it.

**CUSTOMER CHAMPION**

You encourage the people around you to put the customer at the centre of production and purchasing calls, not as an afterthought. You translate customer and demand signals into forecasting, ordering, and capacity decisions the team can act on, and you translate operational reality — what can be built and shipped, and by when — back to Commercial in terms they can take to a customer.

**IMPACT**

You take on the higher-ambiguity work — the ERP, a second production partner, a forecast that has to hold at 500+ units — not only the convenient pieces. You state outcomes, not outputs: what changed in cost, lead time, stock accuracy, or capacity because of your work, published where the company can read it, including when it didn't land. You summarise a problem, your recommendation, and the trade-offs concisely so decisions can be made quickly.

**AGILITY**

You review and improve processes, routines, and tools when they've stopped fitting purpose — manual tracking, ordering rhythms, forecasting cadence. You make decisions in ambiguity — a demand spike, a delayed part, a product version cutover — without pushing uncertainty up or sideways, and you document the trigger, the decision, and the trade-offs. You run changes as tests and share what you learned openly, including when it didn't work.

**INTEGRITY**

You make decisions in public forums, not private channels, and you name what you're holding back and why. You hold peers accountable to commitments in the moment — a forecast sign-off, a delivery date, a handover — and give candid feedback regularly rather than saving it up. You make it safe to flag a missed order, a bad forecast, or a supplier problem early, so it isn't buried.

## Job requirements

**Essential experience**

* 5+ years in supply chain, procurement, or production planning for a business that manufactures a physical product — ideally through a contract manufacturer or production partner rather than an owned factory.
* Has owned a supply chain, procurement, or production planning function end-to-end — not just executed within one — and is comfortable being the senior authority on production, parts, and logistics calls day-to-day, without escalating routine decisions upward.
* Direct experience negotiating supplier and freight/logistics rates, and running shipments across multiple regions (UK, EU, and US at minimum).
* Has implemented and/or owned an ERP or inventory management system, ideally from a low- or no-tooling starting point — including the work after go-live (data quality, adoption, and evolving it as the business scales) — not just used one that was already in place.
* Has worked with third-party logistics providers (3PLs) — contracting them and managing stock held with them against a holding limit, including inventory reporting and reconciliation.
* Comfortable with long-lead-time, capacity-constrained components (electronics, custom hardware) and the forecasting discipline that requires.
* Understands customs, duties, and international shipping documentation (Incoterms, HS codes) for outbound freight to the US, EU, and UK.
* Commercially literate: can read a landed-cost breakdown, model unit economics, and negotiate from an understanding of true cost drivers, not just headline price.
* Comfortable building process from scratch with a small internal team and a single production partner, rather than inheriting an established function.

**Desirable experience**

* Experience scaling production volume materially year-on-year (e.g. low hundreds to low thousands of units), not steady-state manufacturing.
* Familiarity with UK manufacturing and logistics specifically.
* A supply chain or procurement qualification (e.g. CIPS, APICS/CPIM) — application matters more than the certificate.
* Experience evaluating or onboarding a second manufacturing partner, or otherwise multi-sourcing a production line — including in the US market.

**What Success Looks Like**

* 90 days: purchasing and supplier or Iota queries have transferred from the Hardware Manager, and forecasting and budget approval have transferred from the COO. You have a clear, current picture of Iota's committed schedule, the parts pipeline, and finished-goods stock, you've mapped where the 18-week lead time creates real risk against known and forecast demand, and you've taken over the ERP, assessed it against Greyparrot's actual requirements, and agreed a prioritised roadmap of what to fix or extend.
* 3 months: the ERP is the working system for stock, orders, and production across Operations, Hardware, Finance, and Commercial, with the first items on your roadmap closed or scheduled. Supplier and shipping rates have been renegotiated or benchmarked at least once. A rolling capacity and demand forecast is in regular use by Operations and Commercial. Where stock exceeds Iota’s holding limit, a 3PL arrangement is in place or decided.

* 1 year: production, parts and outbound logistics run to a forecast that holds up under scaling volume. The ERP is the business's single source of truth for stock and production status, with data people trust, and you have a view on whether it scales to 2027 volumes or needs replacing. Evaluation of a second production partner — likely US-based — is underway, as the start of a 2027 move away from single-partner dependency, not a 90-day deliverable.

## **About Greyparrot:**

The world is in a waste crisis.

Currently we produce 2.1 billion tons of solid waste per year. Data collection of the waste we produce is non-existent, meaning no systematic transparency and no accountability. It means that recycling targets are not upheld, dumping of waste into our oceans remains nobody's responsibility, recyclables get sent to landfill or incineration, and producers get away with sub-standard packaging. Thus, recycling rates stubbornly remain at 10% and, unless we change, by 2040 the plastic stock in the ocean will have quadrupled - a problem that already costs society $1.5 trillion each year.

Our mission is to increase transparency and automation in waste management to accelerate the circular economy. # Manager: Compliance Advisory and Data Protection

## **About Griffin**

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

### **Our culture**

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work *and* home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

## **The Team**

You'll join our Service guild and work across first line operations, sales and produt. Working closely with Protect (our second line) you'll be the first person dedicated to compliance within the team. You'll define what great compliance solutions look like. Then implement them , keeping Griffin's products and customer outcomes in shape as we grow.

## **The opportunity**

We want compliance and data protection built into how we design, sell and run our products. As our hands on DPO and compliance adviser, in the first line (the teams who run the business and own its risks), you'll bring regulatory expertise to help our operations, commercial and product teams do exactly that. With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

### **What success looks like**

In your first year, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. And you’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation.

### **To do this you'll be involved in:**

* **Product development:** turning regulation into clear requirements, customer journeys, T&Cs and fair value assessments, from first idea through product approval to launch, with data protection built in from the start.
* **Product lifecycle management:** keeping live products compliant through periodic fair value assessments, outcome monitoring, reviews, changes and closures.
* **Sales:** helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material.
* **Marketing:** working on marketing materials, both ours and our customers’, to make sure they comply with regulation and our own policies, and that our financial promotions are properly challenged.
* **Service (Operations):** building regulatory and data protection requirements into how Service works day to day, with procedures and controls people actually use.
* **Regulatory change:** working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time.
* **Issues and reporting:** investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes.
* **Working with second line (Protect):** bringing them in early, sharing the evidence they need, and acting on their challenge.
* **Data protection:** being our Data Protection Officer (DPO), which means:

  + advising our teams on their obligations, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and transfer risk assessments (TRAs)
  + monitoring and auditing how well we comply with the UK GDPR, other data protection laws and our own policies
  + training colleagues and raising awareness of data protection
  + being our contact point for the ICO and for people with questions or requests about their data

As our DPO, you’ll report directly to our COO and have the independence you need to do the job well. We’ll involve you early in anything that affects personal data.

We expect you to shape this role: This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves is for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where you can make the biggest difference.

**We expect you to shape this role:** This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

## 

## **Your background**

We need a proactive doer. You get stuck in without waiting to be asked, and you’re comfortable tackling regulations you haven’t met before. You use your experience and expertise to help our teams find simple, clear and compliant solutions. Your advice is balanced, easy to follow and focused on the risks that matter most. You want to push the business forward, and you see good compliance as part of how we get there.

To ensure this, we're looking for people who have:

* **Compliance experience** in the first (preferred) or second line of a UK regulated firm, ideally a bank, e-money institution or payments firm.
* **Practical knowledge of the rules behind our products**, like Consumer Duty, BCOBS, CASS, FISMA, the Payment Services Regulations and the Money Laundering Regulations. As well as familiarity with HMRC requirements like BBSI and AEOI reporting.
* **Expert knowledge of data protection law and practice**, including the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, PECR and the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.
* **Hands-on experience turning regulation into practical requirements** for product, sales or operations teams.
* **A curious, questioning approach.** You know the right questions to ask before signing something off, not just the rules to check it against.
* **The confidence to challenge,** clearly and kindly, when something isn’t right.

* **A love of writing**. We have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write).

Ideally, you would also:

* **Have deep expertise in at least one specialist area,** such as payments, cards, Consumer Duty, BCOBS, financial promotions or similar.
* **Have been a DPO,** or worked closely with one, in a regulated firm.
* **Have worked in finance or banking.**

## **What can we offer you?**

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.

* **Salary:** £ 80-90 (DOE)
* **Remote-first flexibility:** Work from anywhere in the UK
* **Work from abroad:** Up to 20 days a year
* **Time off:** 25 days’ holiday, bank holidays and a winter break (we shut down between Christmas and New Year)
* **Share options:** Own a part of what we’re building together
* **Pension:** Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme
* **Insurance:** Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG
* **Wellbeing:** 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva
* **Family leave:** Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service
* **AI tools:** Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools
* **Your setup:** We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

**As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks**

## 

## **How long will the process take?**

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

* **Step 1:** An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience.
* **Step 2:** Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements.
* **Step 3:** A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin.
* **Step 4:** Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview.
* **Step 5**: Culture and Founder interview: Learn more about this here.

## **How do I apply?**

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

### **We’re remote-first**

We trust people to do great work wherever they are. We hire across the UK and most of our team works remotely full-time. We have a small London office in Moorgate for those who want it, and about a third of the company is close enough to use it occasionally, but there's no expectation to be there. What matters is the work, not where you do it.

### **Under representation**

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

# VP of Engineering, Full Stack (CTO Track)

## About the company

We're a frontier AI lab building our own foundation model for safety-critical embedded control software. Think motor controllers, battery management, power electronics and vehicle systems, where a bug is a physical failure, not a 500 error.

Our platform puts that model to work. Its user-facing product is the environment where control engineers specify, generate, review, test and trace embedded software with AI assistance.

Our foundation model is available now. The job is to integrate it into the product and turn it into something engineers trust, on an architecture that takes each new model release without a rewrite.

## The role

You'll be the most senior engineer on the product and the person who decides how it's built. This is a hands-on role: you'll write a large share of the code in year one.

As the product and team grow, you'll grow into technical leadership of the platform, setting architecture, engineering standards and hiring. For the right person, this is a **clear path to CTO**.

You'll work directly with the founding team and the model research team. The bridge between a frontier model and a product that safety-critical engineers rely on runs through you.

**Reports to:** Founders

## What you'll do

* **Architecture:** Own the architecture across frontend, backend, data and infrastructure, and make the build-vs-buy calls.
* **Product delivery:** Ship features fast, working closely with product and early users who are control and embedded engineers.
* **Model integration:** Design the integration layer (inference serving, prompt and context management, tool use, streaming, evaluation hooks and fallbacks) so we integrate our model now and adopt future releases without a rewrite.
* **Trust workflows:** Build what engineers need to trust AI-generated code: traceability from requirements to code, diffing and review, test execution and audit trails.
* **Engineering foundations:** Set up CI/CD, observability, security, access control and cost control for GPU-backed workloads.
* **Enterprise readiness:** Prepare the product for enterprise customers in regulated industries: SSO, data isolation, on-prem or private-cloud deployment.
* **Team:** Hire, mentor and lead the first engineers, and define how the team works.

## What you bring

* 10+ years building and shipping production software, with real depth on both frontend and backend
* Strong TypeScript and React (or equivalent modern frontend), plus at least one backend language such as Python, Go or TypeScript/Node
* Experience as the founding, lead or principal engineer on a product taken from early stage to paying customers
* Hands-on experience shipping LLM-powered features in production: model APIs or self-hosted inference, streaming, evaluation and cost/latency trade-offs
* Solid cloud and infrastructure skills (AWS, GCP or Azure; containers; infrastructure as code)
* Good architectural judgement: you know when to move fast and when the cost of a shortcut is too high
* Experience hiring and leading engineers, or a clear appetite to do so
* Clear written and spoken English, and comfort working directly with founders, researchers and customers

### Nice to have

* Familiarity with safety and quality standards such as SOC 2, ISO 27001 or FedRAMP
* Experience building developer tools, IDEs, code editors (e.g. Monaco, VS Code extensions) or code analysis tooling
* Experience serving custom or fine-tuned models (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Triton or similar) and GPU infrastructure
* Rust or C/C++ experience
* Experience selling to and deploying in regulated or security-conscious enterprises

## What we offer

* CTO-level ownership of a product at the meeting point of frontier AI and real-world engineering
* A clear path to CTO as the company grows
* Competitive salary and meaningful CTO-level equity
* Direct work with a founding team that combines AI research with hands-on experience building high-voltage and electric drive systems
* London office with hybrid working; remote considered for exceptional candidates
* A full benefits package

## Logistics

* **Location:** London preferred (hybrid); exceptional candidates considered globally
* **Type:** Full-time, permanent
